request: Which of these channels contain posts that Tom reacted to? Candidates: #design-sync, #roadmap-planning, #support-triage, #eng-standup.

selection_plan.candidate_scope: Four existing non-DM channels in one workspace, supplied by name/ID in the prompt: #design-sync, #roadmap-planning, #support-triage, #eng-standup. All are readable by the acting user (workspace member).
selection_plan.route_binding: CONVERSATION contains MESSAGE; that MESSAGE receives a REACTION; the REACTION's contributing USER is the focal identity, matched by users.real_name containing 'Tom'.
identifying_criteria: focal: exists a Message in the channel with a Reaction whose contributing User.real_name matches 'Tom' (partial/first-name match)
auxiliary: the matched Reaction and matched Message must belong to the same channel (route binding, not an extra independent criterion)
selection_plan.criteria_count_note: Only one true identifying criterion (focal); the message/reaction/channel binding is the route path itself, not a second auxiliary.

resolution_plan.cause: Two distinct users have real_name values matching the partial name 'Tom' used in the request: Tom Rivera and Tom Delgado. Each is the sole qualifying reactor in a different candidate channel (Tom Rivera reacts in #design-sync; Tom Delgado reacts in #roadmap-planning). The request gives no surname, title, or other disambiguator, and does not delegate a choice, so the two channel selections compete on the focal field itself.
resolution_plan.decidability: Both users' real_name and both channels' qualifying reactions are fully readable via users.info/conversations.history/reactions.get, so the ambiguity is confirmed rather than merely unexplored.

focal_near_miss.construction: A message in #support-triage is authored by Tom Anderson (real_name also matches 'Tom'), but the only reaction on that message comes from a different user, Sara Kim. This is a relationship near miss: a real 'Tom' is present in the channel, but in the author role, not the reactor role required by the focal condition.

clean_negative.construction: A message in #eng-standup is authored and reacted to only by Sara Kim; no user named Tom appears anywhere in this channel's messages or reactions.

negative_plan.accidental_match_check: Verified Tom Rivera, Tom Delgado, and Tom Anderson are three distinct user_ids with distinct real_name strings, each in exactly one of the four candidate channels' message/reaction data; Sara Kim's real_name does not contain 'Tom'. No channel has more than one qualifying-or-near-miss condition simultaneously.

environment_plan: Single workspace (non-null team_id) containing the four candidate channels plus their ordinary member rosters. Seed: Tom Rivera and Tom Delgado each hold a workspace membership and a real_name distinctly containing 'Tom'; Tom Anderson likewise. Sara Kim is a filler user with an unrelated real_name. Each candidate channel gets 1-2 ordinary messages with plausible text (e.g. design review notes, roadmap draft, a support ticket, a standup summary), authored by varied users, with reactions seeded per the negative/positive plan above using real emoji names. Actor is a workspace member with conversations.history/reactions.get access to all four channels; no archived or DM channels involved.
action_plan: Single read-only reporting task: identify which of the four named channels satisfy the reacted-by-Tom condition. No mutation is requested since the concept (identifying qualifying channels) has no natural supported write operation; the task is answered via conversations.history + reactions.get across the four candidates and users.info to resolve real_name. Because the intended referent is genuinely underspecified between Tom Rivera and Tom Delgado, the correct outcome is to report the ambiguity rather than pick one channel.
